messages.subject: Re: Coordinates fall outside polygons
messages.body_plain:
Vicki
The 'traps' input should have the coordinates of the boundary of the polygon that you searched; it is not constructed from the coordinates of the points where you found faeces, as you implied. Perhaps you need to give us some more information.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Coordinates fall outside polygons
messages.body_plain:
Hi
I'm glad you made some progress!

Let me get pedantic on two points: we use 'session' and 'occasion' to mean different things in 'secr' (and Density, where the Help explains this better). I think you mean 'occasion'. Also, case is important in R, and the package is 'secr' (lowercase).

I can't really tell what you've done to combine occasions (would make sense to use 'reduce') or what code you have used to get the error message. Also, it looks like you are trying to use both a mask and a buffer distance; specify just one of these. Again, maybe you need to give us more.

Murray

messages.subject: Minor clash between mixture models and incomplete detector 'usage'
messages.subject_clean: Minor clash between mixture models and incomplete detector 'usage'
messages.body_plain:
Just cross-referencing an obscure phidot <http://www.phidot.org/forum/viewtopic.php?f=36&t=2069> post regarding a bug I found in secr.fit(). Mixture models (including hcov) fail (or complete with a convergence error) when the first trap/camera is not used on the first occasion. There are several workarounds: re-order traps or occasions in the input, simply change the first 'usage' value to 1, or collapse occasions with 'reduce'.
Murray

messages.subject: unstable mask.check value in Exponential detection function
messages.subject_clean: unstable mask.check value in Exponential detection function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Murray & everyone

I'm trying to fit model with exponential detection function, the models were fitted with varies buffer from 10000-25000 m (for half normal 15000 was good enough). "mask.check" showed unstable log likelihoods and spacing, even though I used 25000 m. Should I use "suggest.buffer"? or It was not enough buffer width?

                   model                 detectfn npar    logLik           AIC          AICc       dAICc     AICcwt
fit.Expo        g0~1 sigma~1     exponential      2 -164.5110   333.022    333.451   0.000     0.9091
fit.null          g0~1 sigma~1     halfnormal        2 -166.8136   337.627    338.056   4.605     0.0909

I expected exponential detection in disturbed forest for bears, and half normal for undisturbed forest.

Thanks,
Dusit

messages.subject: Re: unstable mask.check value in Exponential detection function
messages.subject_clean: unstable mask.check value in Exponential detection function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dusit!

We don't have much to go on... In general the exponential has a longer tail, so you might need a wider buffer. But 25 km is a long way, even for a bear... Are you sampling over such a long period that the sample includes home-range shifts or transients?

The real question is whether it matters (i.e. affects the density estimate): suggest.buffer and mask.check only give clues. Have you looked at esa.plot? That gives a quick view of how the estimated density changes as you increase buffer width.

I doubt anyone can predict the effect of habitat on shape of detection function, but I may be wrong.

That's my 2 cents worth.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: unstable mask.check value in Exponential detection function
messages.subject_clean: unstable mask.check value in Exponential detection function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dusit

LIke Murray, I suspect that the shape of the detection function is not really predictable in advance. And depending on your detector density, you may not have much ability to distinguish between shapes on the basis of the capture data (higher detector density gives greater ability). You do however, seem to have good reason to suspect that animal ranges are different in the two habitats, and it these circumstances my starting point would be to use a detection function in which both g0/lambda0 and sigma depend on the mask covariate "habitat type" (or whatever you call it).

You can't use suggest.buffer() etc. with this kind of model, but you can quite easily look into the effect of buffer size by just looping through a series of fits in R, using a model like that above, and increasing buffer size on each fit. If you save the detection function parameter estimates, density and esa estimates inside the loop, you can then construct plots after the loop that show how these estimates change with buffer size and at what buffer size they (hopefully) stop changing much. (If you are not sure how to program this, I can help - or Murray may already have code to hand that does it.)

One thing to bear in mind: I suspect that you might end up needing quite a high-resolution mask (i.e. lots of mask points) because a suitable buffer for the animals with big ranges might give a very big mask for animals with small ranges and if you don't have enough grid points in the mask, it is concievable that you end up with so few grid points per range of the small-range animals that you get too crude an estimate of the small-range animals' esa. (The space that animals actually occupy is continuous - the mask is a discrete approximation to this space and if it is too discrete it can be a poor approximation.)

David

messages.subject: Re: unstable mask.check value in Exponential detection function
messages.subject_clean: unstable mask.check value in Exponential detection function
messages.body_plain:
Hi again
David has a point about the mask possibly getting too coarse as you go to extreme buffer widths (if you don't increase nx or hold spacing constant in make.mask). That at least is an explanation for instability in the mask.check likelihoods.

I suspect that Dusit's habitat patches were discrete study areas (sessions), so it would be simple to handle the habitat variation as session-dependent. 'secr' doesn't normally allow detection parameters (g0/lambda0/sigma) to depend on mask covariates, although there is a trick in the next release that effectively allows sigma to depend on mask covariates. Watch this space.
Murray

messages.subject: secr 2.9.1
messages.body_plain:
A new release of secr is starting to find its way to CRAN mirror sites. Check out the NEWS <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/secr/index.html> for a list of changes. The main feature is flexible machinery for detection models based on non-Euclidean distances, documented in the new vignette secr-noneuclidean.pdf <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-noneuclidean.pdf>. A few bugs are fixed. The 'start' argument of secr.fit() can now be a named list of one or more 'real' parameter values, and there are other labour-saving tweaks.
Murray

messages.body_plain:
John Boulanger has pointed out that group ('g') models do not work in secr 2.9.1 (annoyingly, secr.fit() fits the model and then crashes). Sorry about this. It's a headache to maintain the code for groups, and I seldom use them, but I know other people do and I'll run more checks in future. There is an easy fix - please email me if you need access to an update before I fix it on CRAN.
Murray
